what: Kimi K3 decode kernels. Every dimension is a key from the RELEASED MODEL'S OWN config.json, read 2026-11-02; none is chosen and none is inferred from a tensor shape.
shapes_source: the released model's OWN config.json at moonshotai/Kimi-K3 on Hugging Face, read 2026-11-02. Every value below is a key from that file. This is the first of the two candidate sources the earlier note named, and it is the authoritative one -- an adjacent-generation config from a model zoo would give numbers that are not comparable with these.
source_correction: This entry read `awaiting_source` with the note 'blocked on the file, not only on a decision', on the grounds that no Kimi K3 GGUF is on this machine (the published quant is 94 shards, ~594 GB). That conflated the WEIGHTS with the CONFIGURATION. The shapes live in a 7 KB config.json, and GLM 5.3's came from metadata rather than from tensors too. The block was never the file.
architecture_note: A 69/24 KDA-to-MLA hybrid over 93 blocks, one of them dense. Two things separate it from GLM 5.3 and both change what the corpus can hold. (1) `hidden_act` is `situ`, not SwiGLU, carrying two beta parameters -- so the dense FFN and the expert FFN are NOT expressible here, where GLM 5.3's were. (2) N_EXP is 896 = 7 x 128, so the expert count DOES admit f32 tiling, where GLM 5.3's 288 admits none. The router is sigmoid + top-k with `noaux_tc`, not softmax + top-k.

not_in_this_corpus.kda_recurrence: a sequential scan across 69 of 93 blocks; the tile API has no recurrent-scan intrinsic.
not_in_this_corpus.kda_short_conv: a depthwise causal convolution; the tile API has no sliding-window intrinsic.
not_in_this_corpus.situ_ffn: BOTH FFN paths. `hidden_act` is `situ`, not SwiGLU, and the tile API's activation vocabulary is silu / gate_up_silu / sigmoid / exp. This is the one place K3 differs from GLM 5.3 in what can be EXPRESSED rather than in a dimension -- GLM 5.3's SwiGLU FFNs are in that corpus. Emitting gate_up_silu here would report on arithmetic this model does not perform.

representations.tile: generated by bench/shapes/gen_kimi_k3.py from the registry's sourced shapes.
representations.pto: from the in-tree rspto. Reproducible; a test asserts it byte for byte.
representations.tile-rs: lifted from the .pto by the in-tree ptoas-rs. Compiled, and checked to still be producible from its own .pto.
representations.searched: for a refused kernel, the tiling tile-search chose instead. Two entries: the argmax, rescued from a 163840 extent to 20480 against the PTO emitter, and the output projection, rescued from 7168 to 3584 against the AscendC emitter -- which needed `--oracle ascendc`, because its refusal was invisible to the default one.

totals.device_verified_what_it_counts: COUNTS rows in THIS corpus carrying a device_check with no outstanding attribution caveat, of any date. It is NOT the migration campaign's device-verified count, and as of 2026-11-08 the two differ by exactly 13 across the four corpora -- 46 rows here against 33 banked -- with every one of the 13 accounted for: 10 are in the `engine` corpus, which is outside the campaign's K=72 scope (deepseek_v41, glm_5_3, kimi_k3) and so is never banked by it; the other 3 are kimi_k3's SiTU gate/up rows, which reproduce their recorded max_rel 4.892e-06 exactly and are held back only because that figure meets the 1e-5 this row declares and not the 1e-6 the campaign's tolerance table assigns to f32_elementwise. See each of those rows' device_check_tolerance_conflict_2026_11_08. A row here claims `this kernel was observed correct on device`; a campaign `verified` record additionally claims `these exact bytes were, at the campaign's own tolerance`. The 2026-11-08 sweep is what made the second claim checkable: 13 artefacts across the tree did not derive from their own .tile, and until model_corpora_ascendc_matches_its_emitter.rs landed, only bench/playground16 was gated.

what_the_refusals_say: Two are specific to THIS MODEL'S DIMENSIONS rather than to the tile API. D is 7168, and a single f32 tile of it overflows the 910b per-buffer budget where GLM 5.3's 4096 fits, so the output projection emits PTO and is refused by the AscendC emitter. VOCAB is 163840 and the argmax over it is refused by both, the PTO side naming the UB working set directly. The third is an emitter gap, not a bound: mlir_to_cpp has no arm for __tile_sigmoid_f32, which the router needs because this model routes with sigmoid rather than softmax, and it refuses rather than dropping the operation silently.

argmax_k3_1x163840.pto_refused: NPU UB budget (arch a2a3): tile of 81920B at offset 164352B would use 246272B > UB_SIZE 194560B (C1); the live tile working set exceeds the Unified Buffer — reduce tile shapes or free earlier
argmax_k3_1x163840.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED: the bound was real and the arm did not exist. mlir_to_cpp now has a CHUNKED ARGMAX arm, the fourth rescue and the one the others cannot do -- an argmax carries a PAIR, a running maximum and the index that attained it, and the index's meaning depends on where its chunk started, so neither a tile accumulator nor a wider buffer helps. The emitted argmax block already computes exactly the per-chunk partial needed (ReduceMax for the value, one scalar pass for the first index attaining it), so the arm runs it verbatim per chunk (16 x 10240) and adds a pairwise reduce with the chunk base added back. Was: UB overflow in kernel 'k3_argmax_163840': buffer 0 needs 163840 elements (655360 bytes), which is larger than the ENTIRE 188416 byte unified buffer. No division of the budget can hold this tile -- it has to be streamed from global memory in chunks, and mlir_to_cpp has no blocked path for this operat
argmax_k3_1x163840.ascendc_index_is_typed_now: The same change retired this kernel's TILE_SUBSTITUTION. Its .tile declared __tile_store_f32 for an argmax INDEX, so the AscendC arm had to write `replacement=f32-index-storage; reason=u32-buffer-typing-unavailable` -- a marker about a choice the emitter never made, since the source asked for the f32. The generator now declares __tile_store_i32, mlir_to_cpp has that store (it already existed in mlir_to_pto), and the index buffer is typed int32_t, so the store arm's dtype check enforces the pair instead of a comment describing it. Under the migration campaign's eligibility clause the marker capped this kernel at `tiled` whatever a device run said; there is now nothing to cap.
argmax_k3_1x163840.device_check: PASS 2026-11-08 on 910B2 (CANN 8.5.2 aarch64, dav-2201), ORACLE 41 (argmax index, tie policy = lowest index attaining the maximum), n=163840, two identical runs: want=54613 got=54613 EXACT, max=1.000000e+03, ties=2, position=0.333 of n. The POSITION and TIES figures are the evidence that the chunked carry was exercised rather than bypassed: the maximum sits in chunk 5 of 16, so a kernel that forgot the chunk base would have returned 3413, and the deliberate second maximum at 2n/3 means a carry using >= instead of > would have returned 109226. Both are refuted, not merely unobserved.

embedding_k3_163840x7168.pto_refusal_retracted_2026_11_10: RETRACTED: the op existed and the ARM did not. The old text read -- mlir_to_pto has no arm for `__tile_get_value_f32`. The kernel is a GM row copy and the scalar read-back is the one step this emitter cannot take; the AscendC column carries it. Emitting it anyway would drop the operation silently. -- and its premise, that the scalar read-back is a step this emitter cannot take, was about the emitter and read as if it were about PTO. `ptoas` ships as a Python package, so its op registry is inspectable, and `ptoas/mlir/dialects/_pto_ops_gen.py:22306` has declared `pto.tgetval(src, offset) -> value` all along. It never appears in the corpus's .pto vocabulary because nothing had emitted it -- scraping the corpus for the dialect's ops is a narrowing query, and it returned a plausible absence. mlir_to_pto now has arms for `__tile_get_value_f32` -> `pto.tgetval` and `__tile_load_at_f32` -> a runtime-offset `partition_view`, plus `llvm.mul` on a runtime scalar -> `arith.muli`. Operand and result types were MEASURED, not inferred: of five plausible spellings exactly one assembles (offset `index`, result `f32`). The offset is converted to an integer BEFORE the multiply, so unlike the AscendC path it carries no float-exactness bound on the row width. Inertness: 75 of 75 pre-existing .pto regenerate byte-identically, 0 changed.
embedding_k3_163840x7168.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED 2026-11-08: the bound was real and the LOWERING was wrong. `__tile_embedding_f32` declares its weight table as a tile, so no arm can satisfy it at vocabulary scale -- but the operation does not need that intrinsic. At decode shape it is one row copy from GM: read the index, multiply by the row width, `__tile_load_at_f32` at that element offset. The generator now emits that form and this emitter takes it, with the offset reaching the generated `DataCopy(buf1, gm0Tensor[__v3], ...)` so the table is never resident. Kept rather than deleted so the refusal that licensed `ascendc: null` also records its retirement. Was: UB overflow: `__tile_embedding_f32` gathers rows from a tile that holds `dim` element(s) while the vocabulary needs `vocab * dim`. The table cannot be resident, so its rows must be copied from global memory one at a time, and `mlir_to_cpp` has no GM-driven embedding path.

rope_k3_1x64.pto_parent_view_widened_2026_11_08: Re-emitted 2026-11-08 through a WIDENED parent view. The halves formulation loads %arg0 at 0 and at 32, and rspto declares a buffer's view with the shape of the FIRST tile taken from it, so the second load partitioned outside a 1x32 parent. That artefact was briefly stored and three tools disagreed about it: the byte-identity gate PASSED (it compares the emitter against its own output), ptoas-rs refused the lift, and ptoas refused to assemble with 'offset+size at dim 0 (2) exceeds static source dim (1)' -- caught only by stored_pto_assembles.rs. mlir_to_pto's `contain_pv` now re-declares the parent wide enough (2x32, stride 32) instead, because the buffer really is that big and the emitter had simply never said so. No other artefact's bytes moved and no pinned corpus count moved.
rope_k3_1x64.substitution_resolved_2026_11_08: RESOLVED 2026-11-08 (iteration 33). This row carried `TILE_SUBSTITUTION: intrinsic=__tile_rope_f32; replacement=identity-copy; reason=missing-cos-sin-operands` and was ineligible above `tiled`. The substitution is GONE: the generator (bench/shapes/gen_kimi_k3.py) now emits the halves formulation in primitives -- out_lo = x_lo*cos - x_hi*sin, out_hi = x_hi*cos + x_lo*sin -- over FOUR pointers, the chain the engine's verified rope_halves_engine_1x64 uses. `grep -c TILE_SUBSTITUTION` on the artefact is now 0, and no emitter change was needed; the defect was the generator calling a stub intrinsic that has no cos/sin operands. The 2026-11-07 proof trace (pto-models-0001 traces/0003) measured the old identity artefact at wrong=62 of 64 elements, max_rel=3.206e+01 against this same ORACLE 12 -- 32x wrong, not a rounding question -- so any earlier PASS for this kernel would have been against an oracle that does not compute RoPE. deepseek_v41/rope_v41_8x64 is NOT fixed by this and still carries the substitution: at 8 rows the halves sit `cols` apart and need a STRIDED load that __tile_load_f32 does not have, so the generator now REFUSES a multi-row rope rather than emitting a wrong decomposition.

router_sigmoid_topk_k3_1x896_k16.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED: the arm did not exist and now does. mlir_to_cpp gains __tile_sigmoid_f32 and __tile_topk_f32. Top-k is k selection passes of ReduceMax plus a scalar first-hit scan, masking each taken position out of a WORKING COPY so the source survives -- it is read twice in the sigmoid variant. The k VALUES leave through the kernel's own store and the k INDICES through the GM pointer the intrinsic takes as its third operand, as int32, the same decision as the argmax index. Was: mlir_to_cpp has no arm for `__tile_sigmoid_f32`. Emitting it would drop the operation silently: the dispatch skips calls it does not match, so the kernel would compile, run, and quietly omit this step.
router_sigmoid_topk_k3_1x896_k16.ascendc_sigmoid_form: 1/(1+exp(-g)), not e^g/(1+e^g). The short form overflows in f32 past g ~ 88.7 and returns NaN; this one saturates to 1 and 0 at the ends. Not a guess: the K3 SiTU kernels were changed to exactly this chain on 2026-11-05 for that reason and all three are device-verified, so the error this arm carries is one already measured on this part.
router_sigmoid_topk_k3_1x896_k16.device_check: PASS 2026-11-08 on 910B2 (CANN 8.5.2 aarch64, dav-2201), ORACLE 43 (sigmoid then top-k: the k indices, descending by value, ties by LOWER index first), k=16 passed as MV_N, two identical runs: elements=16 wrong=0, want[0..3]=448,224,672,393 got[0..3]=448,224,672,393 EXACT, spread=786 of n=896, ties_at_top=1. The SPREAD is the evidence that this is a selection and not a head extract -- the PTO column's own fallback for this intrinsic is documented as 'a head extract and not a sort', which would have reported spread=15. ties_at_top=1 is the control that the input stayed inside the sigmoid's responsive range; a saturating input flattens the ranks that are supposed to discriminate.
router_sigmoid_topk_k3_1x896_k16.device_check_not_covered: The k VALUES through gm1. This kernel has two outputs and at KERNEL_ARGS == 3 the harness copies back gm2 alone, so the indices are compared and the value store is not. The indices identify the selection completely and the value written is the same one the index was found for, so what is unchecked is whether it reached the right slot of the other buffer. Widening the copy-back would overwrite `b`, which several existing oracles read as an INPUT, so it is not a change an added oracle may make. The oracle PRINTS this line on every run rather than leaving it to be discovered.

what_tile_search_cannot_do:
tile-search decides candidates by running an emitter, and WHICH emitter is now a choice (`--oracle pto|ascendc`) because the two do not agree: the AscendC emitter divides the Unified Buffer into fixed slots, so its limit is per BUFFER where the PTO emitter's is over the live working set. With only the PTO oracle, a kernel refused downstream reported 'nothing to change' -- the right answer to the wrong question.

What remains beyond it is a MISSING EMITTER ARM rather than a bound. The router needs __tile_sigmoid_f32, which mlir_to_cpp does not have, and no tiling supplies a missing arm. One kernel here, and the search says so rather than reporting nothing to change.

estimated_decode_kernels.source: derived from the model's own configuration by inventory(); a LOWER BOUND, because the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.what_it_is: The number of distinct kernels one decode step of this model needs -- the denominator the representation counts are read against. Where the count is KNOWN it is used; where it is not, inventory() derives a LOWER BOUND from the model's own configuration. Not a measurement of a running engine in either case.
estimated_decode_kernels.derivation_error: the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.a_kernel_is: one distinct (operation, shape) pair, because that is what this corpus holds -- one rmsnorm file serves every block that shares D. A layer count does not multiply it.

inventory.line: rmsnorm at D (attn_norm, ffn_norm and the final norm share it)
MLA projections: q_a, q_b, kv_a, kv_b, output
second attention core: the gated delta net
routed expert gate/up at MOE_INTER, and down at D
the leading dense blocks' gate/up at DENSE_FFN_INTER, and down at D

estimated_decode_kernels.reconciliation: 11 kernels present + the rows named above = the DERIVED inventory total of 21. It does not reconcile against 21 when that is a lower bound from another source, and it is not meant to: the gaps were enumerated against the inventory.

what_the_inventory_collapses.each expert's gate, up and down are one: a real engine has three kernels there, and the gate/up pair is often fused separately from the down-projection
what_the_inventory_collapses.one attention core: decode, prefill and partial/chunked are different kernels with different shapes, and a model with two attention types doubles that again
what_the_inventory_collapses.one matvec per projection: f16 and f32 weight forms are separate kernels, and each quantisation the engine supports adds another (q8_0, q4_K, iq2_xxs, mxfp4 ...)
what_the_inventory_collapses.no prefill shapes: every projection and norm has a batched prefill form, which is a different kernel from its decode form
what_the_inventory_collapses.no quantise/dequantise kernels: activation quantisation and weight unpacking are real kernels; the inventory treats weight format as out of scope
what_the_inventory_collapses.one sampling kernel: argmax is counted; top-p, top-k sampling and draft verification are not

estimated_decode_kernels.why_collapses_are_listed_not_multiplied: 'under-counts by 3.5x' is one number and tells a reader nothing they can act on. These name the specific rows that each stand for several real kernels. They are not multiplied out: that would turn a list of known omissions into a fabricated total. Someone who knows the true count for this model can see which rows to expand.
estimated_decode_kernels.published_registry: the published kernel registry, read 2026-11-02, lists ten models and none of them is this one. It has nothing to say here, and a recorded 0 would read as a measurement of zero rather than an absence. The derived lower bound stands unchallenged.
estimated_decode_kernels.note: 28 since 2026-11-06: the estimator rule now counts the seven KDA projections (q, k, v to 8192; two low-rank gate down-projections at 128; their two up-projections). Kimi K3 is 69 KDA blocks of 93, so it needs them at least as much as GLM 5.3 does; they are NOT yet emitted into this corpus, so its corpus is 7 short of the estimate -- which is the allowed direction.

stored_pto_that_does_not_assemble.pto/router_sigmoid_topk_k3_1x896_k16.pto: the stored .pto does NOT assemble: `pto.tci` emits `{descending = ...}` inside the `ins(...)` operand list, where MLIR's parser wants `:`, so ptoas reports `expected ':'`. The attribute belongs on the op. The artefact is kept because it is the reproduction; the byte-identity gate cannot see this, since it compares the emitter's output to the file the emitter wrote and both hold the same invalid text.
